newsitem.title: USA: Russian aluminum exports to fall in 1998 - Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Russian aluminum exports to fall in 1998 - Morgan.

text.p: Improved aluminum demand in the West and stabilisation in Russian exports, which are set to drop in 1998, will combine to push up metal prices, equity analyst Wayne Atwell of Morgan Stanley said.
"We see graphic evidence that aluminum demand is improving and believe that aluminum exports from Russia could decline modestly this year and more materially next year," Atwell said in a report.
"This concept does not appear to be factored into the price of primary aluminum or the aluminum shares," Atwell added.

Morgan Stanley reiterated its strong buy recommendation on aluminum shares for Alcoa (target $80), and Reynolds Metals (target $74), and outperform for Century Aluminum (target $24), and Alumax (target $44).
Morgan said apparent aluminum consumption was flat last year with actual consumption up one to 1.5 percent, adjusting for consumer inventory liquidation.
"We look for no consumer inventory liquidation this year and four-to-five percent real consumption growth followed by three percent growth next year," Atwell said.
Some one million tonnes of primary aluminum capacity is idled in the West, controlled by Alcoa, Alcan, Reynolds and Pechiney.
"We believe this capacity will come back on line at the end of 1997," Atwell said.
